body.estimand_functional: \(\Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}})=s-\prod_{c\in\mathcal C_G}(\mathcal P_c^+\cup\mathcal P_c^-)\) on the joint-margin-preserving nonsingular Gaussian completion family

sampling_model.design: Independent sampling within each row of a fixed-dimensional triangular array.
sampling_model.units: \(O_{n1},\ldots,O_{nn}\sim P_n\), with setting indicators and the observations required for short and supershort regressions.
sampling_model.treatment: Each setting has a real-valued treatment entering the partially linear causal coefficient \(\theta_i(P_n)\).
sampling_model.overlap: The residual treatment variances used by the regular map \(\Gamma\) are uniformly positive; no positivity condition is imposed on any supershort coefficient change \(d_i(\mu_n)\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate the undivided primitive moment \(\mu_n\) by \(\bar h_n\), form \(\widetilde\Omega_n=\widehat\Omega_n+\lambda_n I_p\) with deterministic \(\lambda_n\downarrow0\), and map every accepted primitive vector through the componentwise polynomial sensitivity solver. On a fixed strict regular cell, estimate the endpoint Jacobian with Hong--Li finite perturbations; near zero coordinates or branch and basis ties, retain primitive-set inversion.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The true vector belongs to the polytope formed by the individual and pairwise difference bounds.
The conditional identified set is obtained by slicing the reported joint set at a fixed effect value.
Assumption 4 restricts bias ratios conditionally through ratios of short-minus-supershort coefficient changes.
The reported nonparametric treatment-effect bounds are the tightest possible given the observed assignment, treatment, and response distribution.
Rationalizability is equivalent to membership of observed choice probabilities in a finite generated cone.
Compatibility is characterized by finitely many inequalities and computationally efficient inclusion checks.
Calibrated projection confidence intervals control asymptotic coverage uniformly over a large class of data-generating processes.
With a Gaussian limit, ordinary bootstrap consistency requires full differentiability of the transformation.
Numerical directional differentiation yields consistent inference for directionally differentiable maps under an appropriate step-size sequence.
Joint-test inversion gives identification-robust simultaneous confidence sets for finitely many parameter ratios.
Observed explanatory-power restrictions yield sharp single-setting OVB bounds for broad causal functionals.

body.tldr: Positive bounded ratios of omitted-variable biases do more than bound pairwise bias differences: on every connected setting graph they force one globally compatible, common-sign bias vector, with the all-zero vector as a closure face. The sharp effect set is therefore the affine image of a product of two-polyhedron unions, not the single bias-difference polytope in HuntingtonKlein2026, Proposition 4 on p. 13. The paper proves both inclusions and exhibits a joint-margin-preserving Gaussian latent-control augmentation for every feasible bias vector; arbitrary observed laws receive containment only, while reverse attainment is confined to the nonsingular jointly Gaussian family with unrestricted admissible cross-setting covariance. It also derives closure-complete log-cycle and Farkas certificates, gives equivalent branch-LP and zero-safe MILP computations including an exact fixed-zero rational check, proves a symbolic support gap, and solves a three-setting equality cycle with two simultaneous pins and an exact \(a/2\) outer-slice gap. For estimated supershort calibration it defines a componentwise undivided polynomial sensitivity region. Total regularized primitive-moment inversion supplies supporting uniform coverage at exact-zero and \(n^{-1/2}\)-weak coefficient changes, while a headline regular-cell theorem gives a stable \(C^1\) endpoint map, its Gaussian limit, consistent Hong--Li numerical derivatives, and pointwise first-order equivalence to the known-cell oracle. The genuinely open frontier is a single data-dependent procedure that combines singular-sequence uniform validity with this pointwise oracle recovery.

project_justification.gap: HuntingtonKlein2026, Assumption 3 on pp. 8--9, imposes positive cross-setting bias ratios with intervals containing one, while Proposition 4 on p. 13 reports a polytope built from separately extremized bias differences and Definition 3 on p. 15 pins that outer set. The paper does not prove equality or converse attainment, and Assumption 4 on pp. 17--18 uses divided supershort ratios without sampling inference at weak denominators.
project_justification.niche: Applied researchers need the exact joint set generated by one latent bias vector, certificates that distinguish genuine incompatibility from a numerical artifact, exact answers after several effects are pinned, and confidence sets that remain valid when the data do not identify a supershort ratio.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies an if-and-only-if componentwise sign union with a joint-margin-preserving Gaussian latent augmentation, exact primal--dual computation including fixed-zero strata, analytic support and pin gaps from the published outer polytope, and a solved three-setting cycle. For the undivided supershort sensitivity region, primitive inversion is retained as a supporting uniform-coverage lemma and a separate regular-cell theorem derives endpoint differentiability, a Gaussian limit, consistent numerical derivatives, and pointwise known-cell oracle equivalence. A single procedure that adapts between these regimes remains the first-class open problem.

body.related_work: HuntingtonKlein2026 is the theorem-level comparator. Assumption 3 on pp. 8--9 imposes bounded positive bias ratios with \(\ell_{jk}\le1\le u_{jk}\), and Proposition 4 on p. 13 gives membership in the resulting pairwise bias-difference polytope. Theorem 1 identifies the exact componentwise sign union and proves converse attainment only on the stated nonsingular jointly Gaussian observed-law family with unrestricted admissible cross-setting covariance, while arbitrary observed laws retain containment. The project-maintained generalization permits calibrated ratio intervals that need not contain one. Theorem 3 proves strict tightening of the published outer polytope throughout its stated symmetric family \(a>0\), \(R>1\), and Theorems 4--5 show that slicing as in Definition 3 on p. 15 can overstate a pinned endpoint by exactly \(a/2\). Assumption 4 on pp. 17--18 motivates, but does not state, the project-maintained componentwise polynomial supershort region; Lemma 2 gives its exhaustive zero-coordinate interpretation. BalkePearl1997 informs the converse-attainment standard. ChernozhukovEtAl2026 supplies the single-setting OVB decomposition and efficient estimation of observed sensitivity components, but does not impose cross-setting ratio closure. CinelliHazlett2020 and Oster2019 motivate the observable benchmarking primitives used by supershort calibration. KitamuraStoye2018 informs the finite primal--dual compatibility architecture, and GalichonHenry2011 informs finite separating inequalities; neither studies a positive-OVB-ratio sign union or its zero closure. KaidoMolinariStoye2019 informs repeated feasibility inversion for projected partially identified parameters; Lemmas 3--4 isolate the standard probabilistic work as fixed-dimensional primitive coverage, covariance consistency, and regularized Slutsky equivalence, with deterministic union inclusion thereafter. FangSantos2019 explains the failure of ordinary bootstrap inference at branch or basis ties. HongLi2018 informs the finite-perturbation derivative in Theorem 6, which instead proves pointwise regular-cell basis stability, differentiability, a Gaussian endpoint law, and first-order equality with the known-cell oracle. BolducKhalafYelou2010 and Dufour1997 explain why divided-ratio Wald inference is unsuitable near zero. AndrewsMikusheva2016 informs the open goal of combining weak-regime validity with strong-regime precision in one data-dependent procedure. These method ancestors do not contain the sharp OVB closure or the stated regular-cell endpoint theorem.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The joint-margin-preserving Gaussian augmentation proves that no uniformly tighter set follows from the stated sensitivity restrictions over the nonsingular jointly Gaussian residualized observed-law family. It does not assert that every arbitrary non-Gaussian observed law admits every feasible long coefficient; universal algebraic containment holds, while pointwise sharp equality is confined to the stated Gaussian family.
body.honest_scope: The theorem claims cover the exact componentwise union, its joint-margin-preserving Gaussian attainment, cycle and Farkas certificates, zero-safe branch-LP or MILP equivalence, symbolic support and pin gaps, the solved three-setting equality cycle, and pointwise regular-cell endpoint oracle recovery. Arbitrary observed laws receive containment only; reverse attainment is confined to the stated nonsingular jointly Gaussian observed-law family with unrestricted admissible cross-setting covariance. The supershort object is a calibrated sensitivity region, not a claimed causal identified set. Uniform primitive inversion is a supporting consequence of primitive-ellipsoid coverage and deterministic union inclusion, not a substantive inversion theorem. One data-dependent procedure that is uniformly valid on singular sequences and oracle-equivalent off them remains open. The attainment sanity reduction holds coordinatewise: for \(B_i\ne0\), the structural equation collapses identically to \(Y_i=s_iD_i+U_i\) and leaves the observed vector untouched, while for \(B_i=0\) it collapses to the ordinary short regression with an independent latent control. Singleton graph components recover the Cartesian product of the published individual OVB intervals, \(R=1\) in the symmetric two-setting family forces equal biases and makes the support gap zero, and away from zero denominators the polynomial supershort restriction reduces to the reciprocal-ratio interval.
